description:
Amazing books you can finish in a single sitting.

All books available at the @paintedporchbookshop
transcript: amazing books you can read in a single sitting. The War of Art, I try to read it before I start any creative project. Seneca's essay on the shortness of life, one of the greatest pieces of philosophy ever written. It's not that life is short, he says, it's that we waste a lot of it. Zen and the Art of Archery, another amazing philosophy book from the other side of the world. This is the new Walter Isaacson book, The Greatest Sentence Ever Written, about the first sentence of the Declaration of Independence. A nice 70 page or so meditation on a wonderful sentence and what it means 84 charring cross road you will fall in love with all the characters in this book and devour it in one setting this little book i loved it so much i bought a thousand copies of it and i think we're one of the only bookstores in the country that has it this is a little book by stefan's wife who wrote the world of yesterday it's just a short biography of montaaigne. He's writing as the world is falling apart and he's writing about a guy, Montaigne, who is writing and thinking when his world is falling apart. It's a lovely book. Gift from the Sea by Anne Morrow Lindbergh. It's a lady walking along a beach writing on youth, age, love, and marriage, peace, solitude, and contentment. She writes this on a brief vacation and it's kind of a vacation of a book to read. The Boy, the Fox, the Horse and the Mole. This is one I read to my kids. It's just the right length. This one's almost too short to be a book but it is in fact a book. This is Stockdale's Courage Under Fire. This is a man testing the doctrines of Epictetus in the Hanoi Hilton as a prisoner of war in Vietnam. Meditations is technically 170 pages. You can read it in one sitting, you're not supposed to. I prefer to flip through it. I think this is a one sitting book, but this is a book you should be sitting with over and over and over again over the course of your life. Claire Keegan's Small Things Like These. I'll get one novel in here. This book is 114 pages, but it is incredible. The ending, it's gonna fuck you up, but it's very good.
